question:
A 40-year-old man with AIDS comes to the physician because of a 3-week history of intermittent fever, abdominal pain, and diarrhea. He has also had a nonproductive cough and a 3.6-kg (8-lb) weight loss in this period. He was treated for pneumocystis pneumonia 2 years ago. He has had skin lesions on his chest for 6 months. Five weeks ago, he went on a week-long hiking trip in Oregon. Current medications include efavirenz, tenofovir, and emtricitabine. He says he has had trouble adhering to his medication. His temperature is 38.3°C (100.9°F), pulse is 96/min, and blood pressure is 110/70 mm Hg. Examination shows oral thrush on his palate and a white, non-scrapable plaque on the left side of the tongue. There is axillary and inguinal lymphadenopathy. There are multiple violaceous plaques on the chest. Crackles are heard on auscultation of the chest. Abdominal examination shows mild, diffuse tenderness throughout the lower quadrants. The liver is palpated 2 to 3 cm below the right costal margin, and the spleen is palpated 1 to 2 cm below the left costal margin. Laboratory studies show:
Hemoglobin 12.2 g/dL
Leukocyte count 4,800/mm3
CD4+ T-lymphocytes 44/mm3 (Normal ≥ 500 mm3)
Platelet count 258,000/mm3
Serum
Na+ 137 mEq/L
Cl- 102 mEq/L
K+ 4.9 mEq/L
Alkaline phosphatase 202 U/L
One set of blood culture grows acid-fast organisms. A PPD skin test shows 4 mm of induration. Which of the following is the most appropriate pharmacotherapy for this patient's condition?"?
reasoning_chain: CHAIN: "Patient has AIDS" -> "CD4+ T-lymphocyte count is 44/mm3" -> "indicates severe immunosuppression" -> "increased risk for opportunistic infections" -> "intermittent fever, abdominal pain, diarrhea, cough" -> "oral thrush indicates possible candidiasis" -> "acid-fast organisms in blood culture" -> "suggests possible mycobacterial infection" -> "PPD skin test shows 4 mm induration" -> "indicates possible latent tuberculosis" -> "most appropriate treatment includes azithromycin and ethambutol for mycobacterial infection" -> 85%

CHAIN: "Patient presents with fever and weight loss" -> "history of AIDS and low CD4+ count" -> "risk for opportunistic infections" -> "oral thrush suggests candidiasis" -> "skin lesions are violaceous plaques" -> "could indicate Kaposi's sarcoma" -> "blood culture grows acid-fast organisms" -> "suggests mycobacterial infection" -> "PPD skin test shows 4 mm induration" -> "indicates possible exposure to tuberculosis" -> "treatment should include azithromycin and ethambutol" -> 80%

CHAIN: "Patient has a history of AIDS" -> "CD4+ count is critically low" -> "symptoms include fever, cough, and weight loss" -> "oral thrush present" -> "indicates opportunistic infection" -> "blood culture shows acid-fast organisms" -> "suggests mycobacterial infection" -> "PPD skin test shows minimal induration" -> "indicates possible latent TB" -> "azithromycin and ethambutol are appropriate for treatment" -> 75%
analysis: The patient presents with symptoms and findings consistent with disseminated infection, likely due to Mycobacterium avium complex (MAC), given his severely low CD4+ T-lymphocyte count (44/mm3) and the presence of acid-fast organisms in blood cultures. The PPD skin test shows only 4 mm of induration, indicating no significant exposure to tuberculosis. The most appropriate pharmacotherapy for MAC includes azithromycin and ethambutol, which are standard treatments for this opportunistic infection in patients with AIDS. Other options listed do not align with the diagnosis of MAC or are not appropriate for this patient's condition.
